instruction: 3DS export compatibility fix. The input file `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\mesh.dae` is a COLLADA scene that violates two 3DS-format constraints: 1. **Overlong names.** 30 of the 50 `<geometry>` elements carry names longer than 64 characters. Many of those names share an identical 64-character prefix and only differ in the suffix past char 64 - so a naive truncation to 64 characters would produce duplicates. 2. **Quad faces.** 25 of the 50 geometries store their side faces as COLLADA `<polylist>` polygons with `<vcount>` = 4 (quads). The 3DS binary format only stores triangles, so every quad (or n-gon) must be triangulated before export. 1. Read `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\mesh.dae` with any COLLADA parser (e.g. `pycollada`). 2. Triangulate every non-triangular primitive by fan-triangulating each face around its first vertex. 3. Derive a 3DS-safe name for every geometry: - If the original name is <=64 characters, keep it as-is. - Otherwise truncate to 55 characters and append `_` + the first 8 hex digits of the MD5 digest of the *original* name, producing a string exactly 64 characters long. Two long names that share the same 64-char prefix will get different hash suffixes, so uniqueness is preserved. - If a resulting name still collides with another (extremely rare), re-hash with a salt until unique. 4. Write `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\output.3ds` - a valid 3DS binary containing one `NAMED_OBJECT` (chunk id 0x4000) per geometry, each with an `N_TRI_OBJECT` (0x4100) subchunk holding a `POINT_ARRAY` (0x4110) and `FACE_ARRAY` (0x4120). The file must start with the 3DS magic `0x4D4D` in little-endian order. 5. Write `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\name_map.json` - a JSON object mapping every *original* DAE geometry name to its renamed <=64-char string. The map must have exactly 50 entries. Requirements: 1. `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\output.3ds` exists. Its first two bytes are `0x4D 0x4D` (primary chunk magic), and the primary chunk's declared size matches the on-disk file size. 2. The 3DS file contains a `0x3D3D` EDIT3DS chunk with at least 50 `0x4000` NAMED_OBJECT children. 3. Every NAMED_OBJECT name is <=64 characters and all such names are unique within the file. 4. Every NAMED_OBJECT contains an `N_TRI_OBJECT` whose `POINT_ARRAY` and `FACE_ARRAY` payloads are self-consistent (FACE_ARRAY stores exactly 4 uint16 per face - v1, v2, v3, flag - so the format itself guarantees triangles only). 5. `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\name_map.json` exists, is valid JSON, and maps 50 original names to 50 <=64-char strings. 6. All `name_map` values are unique and each value appears as a NAMED_OBJECT name in the 3DS file.
